base_properties.human_readable: Article 112 (Lèse-majesté Laws) as a Legal Mountain

perspectives.label: Thai Citizen
perspectives.comment: From the perspective of an average Thai citizen, Article 112 functions as an immutable law that cannot be easily challenged or changed.

perspectives.label: Thai Judiciary
perspectives.comment: The Thai judiciary, bound by the constitution and legal framework, treats Article 112 as a fundamental legal principle, demonstrating resistance to altering its core tenets.

perspectives.label: External Legal Scholars
perspectives.comment: From a universal legal perspective, Article 112, while controversial, represents a legal structure with a history and deeply entrenched precedents.

commentary.narrative_context: Article 112 of the Thai Criminal Code, which criminalizes insults against the monarchy, functions within the system as a 'Mountain'—a fixed, unchangeable limit. From the perspectives of citizens, the judiciary, and external legal scholars, the law presents substantial resistance to reform or repeal, showcasing its status as a fundamental legal constraint.
key_agents: Thai Citizen: Primary subject (powerless/trapped) — constrained by the law and its potential consequences.
Thai Judiciary: Enforcer (institutional/constrained) — bound by the legal framework to uphold the law.
External Legal Scholars: Observers (analytical/analytical) — analyzing the law within its broad context.
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.10): Low extraction because the law primarily serves as a symbolic measure with few exceptions given in practice. Suppression (0.05): Very low suppression because dissent is easily done in practice. Theater ratio (0.10): Low because it is enforced without fanfare.
commentary.perspectival_gap: There is not significant perspectival gap with the description of Article 112 as a mountain in all described cases.
commentary.directionality_logic: The law primarily extracts from the average Thai citizen, who faces legal repercussions for violations. The judiciary benefits from the law as it maintains stability and order. External legal scholars have an analytical perspective.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The mountain classification indicates that the perspectives view this law as an unchangeable object instead of a construction which would be indicative of a Tangled Rope or Snare classification.
